```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Salem_2023_paclitaxel"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Salem_2023_paclitaxel"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12963> (open access; the Pumas model
  code and fit output are Appendix S1, the equations, Table S1 and Figure S2
  are Appendix S2)

Salem et al. applied published models to first-cycle absolute neutrophil
counts (ANC) taken from electronic health records. Paclitaxel and carboplatin
concentrations were never measured, so both PK layers are fixed literature
models (paclitaxel from Joerger 2006, carboplatin from Joerger 2007), and only
the Friberg myelosuppression parameters were estimated. The packaged model is
this first approach ("PK fixed, PD estimated"), which the authors used for all
downstream analyses.

# Population

The analysis dataset held 405 adults treated at the Inova Schar Cancer
Institute (Fairfax, Virginia) between 2015 and 2019 with weekly paclitaxel
(n = 167), weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin (n = 179) or every-3-weeks
paclitaxel/carboplatin (n = 59) (Table 1). 86.2% were women; 86 patients
(21.2%) were 70 years or older and 20 (5%) were 80 or older. Breast cancer
was the most common primary site (58.7%), followed by ovarian (8.1%) and
non-small cell lung cancer (7.4%). 221 patients reported European ancestry,
55 Asian and 45 African American. The median paclitaxel dose was 80 mg/m^2
in the weekly regimens (1-h infusion) and 175 mg/m^2 every 3 weeks (3-h
infusion); carboplatin was infused over 30 min. Mean baseline ANC was 7.4 and
6.9 x 10^9/L in patients younger and older than 70 years. 2274 ANC values
were analysed (median 5 per patient).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Salem_2023_paclitaxel")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing at its source. The
estimates are taken from the Appendix S1 fit output, which prints them to
more digits than Table S1.

# Typical PK profiles (Figure S2B and S2C)

Figure S2 simulates the typical paclitaxel profile after a 3-h infusion of
175 mg/m^2 and the typical carboplatin profile after a 30-min infusion dosed
to an AUC of 5 mg.min/mL. The typical patient below is a woman with BSA
1.8 m^2, total bilirubin 7 umol/L and age 56 years, the reference values of
the paclitaxel covariate model. Paclitaxel doses enter in umol (molar mass
853.9 g/mol) and carboplatin doses in mg; with the model's fixed carboplatin
clearance of 7.38 L/h (123 mL/min) an AUC of 5 mg.min/mL needs 615 mg.

```{r typical-pk}
mod <- readModelDb("Salem_2023_paclitaxel")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

mw_paclitaxel <- 853.9 # g/mol
umol_paclitaxel <- function(mg) mg / mw_paclitaxel * 1000
cl_carboplatin_ml_min <- 7.38 * 1000 / 60
calvert_mg <- function(auc) auc * cl_carboplatin_ml_min

dose_ptx <- umol_paclitaxel(175 * 1.8)
dose_carb <- calvert_mg(5)

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = 0, amt = dose_ptx, rate = dose_ptx / 3, cmt = "central", evid = 1),
  data.frame(time = 3, amt = dose_carb, rate = dose_carb / 0.5, cmt = "central_carboplatin", evid = 1),
  data.frame(time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), seq(12, 80, by = 0.5)))),
             amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, BSA = 1.8, SEXF = 1, TBILI = 7, AGE = 56) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"))
```

```{r figure-s2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
sim_typ |>
  transmute(
    time,
    `Paclitaxel (umol/L)` = Cc,
    `Carboplatin (mg/L), dosed at t = 3 h` = Cc_carboplatin
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(conc > 1e-3) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "navy") +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S2B (paclitaxel) and S2C (carboplatin) of Salem 2023.")
```

The figure's carboplatin panel starts at the carboplatin dose; here the
carboplatin infusion follows the 3-h paclitaxel infusion, so its curve is
shifted by 3 h.

## PKNCA comparison with Figure S2

The reference values were read by the maintainers from Figure S2: the
paclitaxel peak sits about 0.6 decades above the 1 umol/L gridline (about
4 umol/L), and the carboplatin peak at about 27.5 mg/L. The carboplatin AUC
reference is the dosing target itself (5 mg.min/mL = 83.3 mg.h/L).

```{r pknca-typical}
nca_typ_conc <- bind_rows(
  sim_typ |> transmute(id = 1L, time, Cc, analyte = "paclitaxel"),
  sim_typ |> transmute(id = 1L, time = time - 3, Cc = Cc_carboplatin, analyte = "carboplatin") |>
    filter(time >= 0)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
stopifnot(all(c(0) %in% nca_typ_conc$time))
nca_typ_dose <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = 0, amt = c(dose_ptx, dose_carb),
  analyte = c("paclitaxel", "carboplatin")
)
nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_typ_conc, Cc ~ time | analyte + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_typ_dose, amt ~ time | analyte + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))

published_typ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "paclitaxel", 4.0, NA,
  "carboplatin", 27.5, 5 * 1000 / 60
)
cmp_typ <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_typ,
  reference = published_typ,
  by = "analyte",
  units = c(cmax = "umol/L paclitaxel, mg/L carboplatin",
            aucinf.obs = "umol*h/L paclitaxel, mg*h/L carboplatin"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_typ, caption = "Typical-patient PK: simulated (PKNCA) vs. Figure S2. * differs by > 20%.")
```

```{r typical-checks}
res_typ <- as.data.frame(nca_typ$result)
pk_val <- function(an, p) {
  v <- res_typ$PPORRES[res_typ$analyte == an & res_typ$PPTESTCD == p]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique PKNCA row for ", an, " ", p)
  v
}
# Paclitaxel tail read from Figure S2B: about 0.09 umol/L at 20 h and
# 0.0025 umol/L at 80 h. These are deterministic typical-value solves, so the
# tolerance only has to cover the reading of a log-scale figure.
c20 <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 20]
c80 <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 80]
stopifnot(
  abs(pk_val("paclitaxel", "cmax") / 4.0 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(c20 / 0.09 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(c80 / 0.0025 - 1) < 0.30,
  abs(pk_val("carboplatin", "cmax") / 27.5 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Linear carboplatin: AUC = dose / CL exactly; only integration error remains.
  abs(pk_val("carboplatin", "aucinf.obs") / (dose_carb / 7.38) - 1) < 0.01
)
```

Both typical profiles agree with Figure S2: the paclitaxel peak is
`r signif(pk_val("paclitaxel", "cmax"), 3)` umol/L and the concentration at
20 h is `r signif(c20, 2)` umol/L; the carboplatin peak is
`r signif(pk_val("carboplatin", "cmax"), 3)` mg/L. The carboplatin match is
also the evidence for its concentration unit (see Assumptions).

# Virtual cohort

Patient-level data are not public. The cohort below approximates Table 1:
86% women, BSA about 1.8 m^2 (SD 0.22), total bilirubin log-normal with mean
8.6 umol/L (SD 4.5), and age normal with mean 60 years (SD 12) truncated to
18-90 years, which puts about 20% of patients at 70 years or older (the paper
reports 21.2% but not the mean age). Each regimen gets 150 patients.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2023)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)

n_per_arm <- 150L
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~ptx_mg_m2, ~ptx_inf_h, ~carb_auc, ~dose_days,
  "Weekly paclitaxel", 80, 1, 0, list(c(0, 7, 14, 21)),
  "Weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin", 80, 1, 2, list(c(0, 7, 14, 21)),
  "Every 3 weeks paclitaxel/carboplatin", 175, 3, 5, list(0)
)

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

# Dose and observation rows for one regimen, given one row per subject.
regimen_events <- function(reg, subj) {
  days <- unlist(reg$dose_days)
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(day = days) |>
    mutate(time = day * 24, amt = umol_paclitaxel(reg$ptx_mg_m2 * BSA),
           rate = amt / reg$ptx_inf_h, cmt = "central", evid = 1)
  if (reg$carb_auc > 0) {
    carb <- subj |>
      tidyr::expand_grid(day = days) |>
      mutate(time = day * 24 + reg$ptx_inf_h, amt = calvert_mg(reg$carb_auc),
             rate = amt / 0.5, cmt = "central_carboplatin", evid = 1)
    doses <- bind_rows(doses, carb)
  }
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(12, 28 * 24, by = 6))))
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    select(-any_of("day")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

make_cohort <- function(reg, id_offset) {
  n <- n_per_arm
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    regimen = reg$regimen,
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.862),
    BSA = rtrunc_norm(n, 1.8, 0.22, 1.3, 2.6),
    TBILI = rlnorm(n, log(8.6) - 0.5 * log(1 + (4.5 / 8.6)^2), sqrt(log(1 + (4.5 / 8.6)^2))),
    AGE = rtrunc_norm(n, 60, 12, 18, 90)
  )
  regimen_events(reg, subj)
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(regimens[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "cmt")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$ANC))
```

## ANC over the first month (Figure S4)

```{r figure-s4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(ANC, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(ANC, 0.5), Q95 = quantile(ANC, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (days)", y = "ANC (10^9 cells/L)",
       caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of simulated ANC; compare Figure S4 of Salem 2023.")
```

## Nadir ANC by regimen and age (Figure 3)

The paper reports the mean model-predicted (individual) nadir ANC during the
first month: 2.09, 2.81 and 2.45 x 10^9/L for every-3-weeks
paclitaxel/carboplatin, weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin and weekly paclitaxel,
and 2.6 and 2.4 x 10^9/L for patients younger and older than 70 years.

```{r nadir}
nadir <- sim |>
  group_by(id, regimen, AGE) |>
  summarise(nadir = min(ANC), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(age_group = ifelse(AGE >= 70, ">= 70 years", "< 70 years"))

published_nadir <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~published,
  "Every 3 weeks paclitaxel/carboplatin", 2.09,
  "Weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin", 2.81,
  "Weekly paclitaxel", 2.45
)
nadir_tab <- nadir |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(simulated_mean = mean(nadir), simulated_median = median(nadir), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  inner_join(published_nadir, by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated_mean / published - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(nadir_tab) == 3L)

nadir_tab |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Simulated mean nadir (10^9/L)" = simulated_mean,
    "Simulated median nadir (10^9/L)" = simulated_median,
    "Published mean predicted nadir (10^9/L)" = published,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "First-month nadir ANC by regimen.")
```

The simulated cohort means differ from the published means by
`r round(min(nadir_tab$pct_diff))`% to `r round(max(nadir_tab$pct_diff))`%.
The every-3-weeks regimen gives the deepest nadir in both. Weekly paclitaxel
with and without carboplatin come out almost equal in the simulation, while
the published means put the carboplatin arm higher. The real arms differ in
ways a common virtual cohort does not carry: 24% of the weekly
paclitaxel/carboplatin patients were 70 or older against 14% of the weekly
paclitaxel patients (Table 1), and weekly paclitaxel was the usual breast
cancer regimen while weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin was the usual lung cancer
regimen (Results).

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(nadir, aes(age_group, nadir)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Nadir ANC (10^9 cells/L)",
       caption = "Simulated first-month nadir ANC by age group; compare Figure 3 of Salem 2023.")
```

```{r nadir-checks}
# The cohort mean nadir differs from the published means for reasons that
# move every arm by a similar amount (the virtual cohort's baseline ANC is
# the model's log-normal CIRC0, while the published means are individual
# predictions in the observed cohort), so the gate is on the centre of the
# three differences, not on each arm. A mis-transcribed slope, MTT or dose
# unit moves the nadir by far more than this.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(nadir_tab$pct_diff)) < 30,
  all(nadir_tab$simulated_mean > 0.5), all(nadir_tab$simulated_mean < 6)
)
```

The age effect enters the model only through the paclitaxel VMEL exponent
(-0.352): older patients clear paclitaxel more slowly and so reach a somewhat
lower nadir. The paper's mean predicted nadirs (2.6 vs. 2.4 x 10^9/L below and
above 70 years) and its regression analysis found no meaningful age effect.
For the typical every-3-weeks patient:

```{r age-typical, message = FALSE}
# Typical-value first-month nadir for one regimen: a woman with BSA 1.8 m^2
# and total bilirubin 7 umol/L.
typ_nadir <- function(regimen, age = 56, mod_use = mod_typ) {
  reg <- regimens[regimens$regimen == regimen, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(reg) == 1L)
  subj <- tibble(id = 1L, regimen = regimen, SEXF = 1, BSA = 1.8, TBILI = 7, AGE = age)
  ev <- regimen_events(reg, subj)
  min(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_use, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))$ANC)
}
q3w <- "Every 3 weeks paclitaxel/carboplatin"
age_eff <- c(age50 = typ_nadir(q3w, 50), age80 = typ_nadir(q3w, 80))
age_eff
# Deterministic typical-value solves: the VMEL age exponent moves the nadir
# by well under 1 x 10^9/L across 50-80 years.
stopifnot(abs(age_eff[["age80"]] - age_eff[["age50"]]) < 1)
```

## Literature PD parameters (external-validation approach)

In their second approach the authors fixed the PD parameters as well, to the
literature values that also served as initial estimates in Appendix S1
(CIRC0 4.35 x 10^9/L, MTT 141 h, gamma 0.26, SLOPE 2.08, SLOPEC 0.00162).
They report that both approaches fit the ANC data similarly (Figure S6), with
the estimated slopes about 2.8-fold (paclitaxel) and 3-fold (carboplatin)
higher than the literature values because typical rather than individual PK
was used. The typical nadirs under both parameter sets:

```{r literature-pd, message = FALSE}
mod_lit <- mod_typ |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lcirc0 = log(4.35), lmtt = log(141), gamma = 0.26,
    lslope = log(2.08), lslope_carboplatin = log(0.00162)
  )
lit_tab <- tibble(
  regimen = regimens$regimen,
  estimated = vapply(regimen, typ_nadir, numeric(1)),
  literature = vapply(regimen, typ_nadir, numeric(1), mod_use = mod_lit)
)
lit_tab |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Typical nadir, estimated PD (10^9/L)" = estimated,
    "Typical nadir, literature PD (10^9/L)" = literature
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-patient first-month nadir ANC under the estimated and the literature PD parameters.")
```

# PKNCA of the first paclitaxel and carboplatin doses

The paper reports no NCA. For completeness, the first-week exposure of each
regimen in the virtual cohort:

```{r pknca}
conc_ptx <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 168) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen))
stopifnot(all(tapply(conc_ptx$time, conc_ptx$id, min) == 0))
dose_ptx_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "central", time == 0) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)
nca_ptx <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ptx, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ptx_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

# Carboplatin starts at the end of the paclitaxel infusion; time is taken
# from the carboplatin dose. Its 0.07 h half-life takes the tail into
# integrator noise within a day, where tiny negative values would make the
# log-down trapezoid return NaN, so the tail below 1e-6 of each subject's
# peak is dropped after checking it is noise.
conc_carb <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc_carboplatin), regimen != "Weekly paclitaxel") |>
  mutate(t_carb = time - ifelse(regimen == q3w, 3, 1)) |>
  filter(t_carb >= 0, t_carb <= 167) |>
  transmute(id, time = t_carb, Cc = Cc_carboplatin, regimen = as.character(regimen))
stopifnot(all(conc_carb$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(conc_carb$Cc)))
conc_carb <- conc_carb |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  ungroup()
dose_carb_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "central_carboplatin", time < 168) |>
  mutate(time = 0) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)
nca_carb <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_carb, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_carb_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
# Linear carboplatin: AUC = dose / CL for every subject; only integration
# error separates them.
res_carb <- as.data.frame(nca_carb$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  inner_join(dose_carb_df |> select(id, amt), by = "id")
stopifnot(nrow(res_carb) == 2L * n_per_arm,
          max(abs(res_carb$PPORRES / (res_carb$amt / 7.38) - 1)) < 0.01)

summarise_nca <- function(res, analyte) {
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
    mutate(analyte = analyte, .before = 1)
}
bind_rows(summarise_nca(nca_ptx, "paclitaxel (umol/L, umol*h/L)"),
          summarise_nca(nca_carb, "carboplatin (mg/L, mg*h/L)")) |>
  rename(
    Analyte = analyte, Regimen = regimen,
    "Median Cmax" = cmax, "Median AUClast (first dose)" = auclast, "Median Tmax (h)" = tmax
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Median first-week NCA in the virtual cohort.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Carboplatin concentration unit.** Table S1 labels the carboplatin slope
  SLOPEC in L/umol, but Figure S2C plots the authors' simulated carboplatin
  profile in mg/L, and that profile is reproduced here only when carboplatin
  doses and concentrations are in mg and mg/L (a 615 mg dose for AUC 5 gives a
  peak of about 29 mg/L, against about 27.5 mg/L in the figure; in umol the
  peak would be about 2.7-fold higher). The maintainers therefore treat the
  carboplatin dose as mg and SLOPEC as L/mg, and read the Table S1 unit as
  carried over from the paclitaxel row. If the fit actually used molar
  carboplatin concentrations, multiply SLOPEC by 371.25 / 1000 (that is,
  give doses in umol) to recover it. Paclitaxel is in umol and umol/L in both
  Table S1 and Figure S2B, and its fixed PK parameters are stated in umol.
- **Sign of the saturable transfer in the central-compartment equation.**
  Appendix S2 Eq. 1 prints the central -> first-peripheral Michaelis-Menten
  term with a plus sign; the Appendix S1 code, which is what was fitted,
  subtracts it, and only that form conserves mass. The model follows the code.
- **No paclitaxel or carboplatin IIV.** As in the source, both PK layers are
  typical-value models with covariates; the authors deliberately used typical
  rather than individual PK because no concentrations were measured.
- **The drug effect is not bounded.** `edrug = 1 - SLOPE * C` becomes negative
  at paclitaxel concentrations above 1 / 5.82 = 0.17 umol/L, which every
  regimen exceeds near the end of the infusion. This is the source's
  linear model; proliferation then simply turns into net loss.
- **Regression analysis not encoded.** Table 2 relates the post hoc random
  effects and nadirs to baseline ANC and regimen with a stepwise linear
  regression. Those are summaries of individual estimates, not covariates of
  the fitted model, and are not part of the packaged model.
- **Virtual cohort and dosing.** The paper gives Table 1 summaries by age
  group only, so the age distribution (normal, mean 60, SD 12, truncated
  18-90 years) and the bilirubin distribution are maintainers' choices. Carboplatin
  doses are not reported; the cohort uses AUC 2 weekly and AUC 5 every three
  weeks, dosed against the model's fixed carboplatin clearance. Weekly
  regimens are dosed on days 0, 7, 14 and 21 and the every-3-weeks regimen on
  day 0, and the nadir is the minimum over 28 days. Carboplatin starts at the
  end of the paclitaxel infusion.
- **Nadir comparison.** The published nadirs are means of individual
  predictions in the real cohort, whose mean baseline ANC (about 7.3 x
  10^9/L) differs from the cohort simulated from the model's CIRC0
  distribution; the comparison is a plausibility check on the centre, not a
  reproduction of individual fits.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-10-26.
